task: Write a naturally short recorded telephone greeting for a fictional hall's lost-property service, roughly 45–75 words. Help callers know what to leave and when messages are checked. Do not invent a telephone number, a round-the-clock service, or a promise that an item has been found.

facts.text: Volunteers answer the lost-property line on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 2–4 p.m.
Outside those sessions, callers may leave a message.
Messages are checked at the next volunteer session.
A message should include a callback number and a description of the missing item.
Leaving a description does not establish that the item is in lost property.

forbidden_additions: Daily or immediate message checks, a guaranteed callback time, or twenty-four-hour staffing.
A claim that a caller's item has already been found.
A real telephone number or an invented alternative collection service.
preserve: Volunteer sessions distinguished from the availability of voicemail.
The information needed to investigate rather than a recovery guarantee.
A greeting that can be understood when heard once.
